q: Before accepting a new audit engagement, a successor auditor obtains the prospective client's permission and makes inquiries of the predecessor auditor under AU-C 210. Which of the following matters is the successor required to include in those inquiries?
choices: The predecessor's assessed level of control risk for each significant account
The predecessor's understanding of the reasons for the change in auditors
The audit fees the predecessor charged in each of the last two years
The sample sizes the predecessor used for its tests of controls
exp: AU-C 210 requires inquiries about management integrity, disagreements with management, communications with those charged with governance about fraud, noncompliance and internal control matters, and the predecessor's understanding of the reasons for the change. Detailed risk assessments and sample sizes come from a working-paper review after acceptance, not from the required pre-acceptance inquiries.

q: A prospective audit client refuses to permit the successor auditor to communicate with the predecessor auditor. Under AU-C 210, the successor auditor should
choices: accept the engagement but issue a qualified opinion on opening balances
contact the predecessor anyway, because the communication is required by GAAS
decline the engagement, because GAAS prohibits acceptance in this situation
inquire about the reasons for the refusal and consider the implications in deciding whether to accept the engagement
exp: When a prospective client refuses permission, the successor should ask why and weigh the implications for acceptance (AU-C 210). Declining is not automatically required, and contacting the predecessor without permission would breach the predecessor's confidentiality obligations.

q: During acceptance discussions, management states that it will not allow the auditor to send confirmations to any customers or to observe the physical inventory count, which together are material and pervasive to the financial statements. No law or regulation requires the audit. Under AU-C 210, the auditor should
choices: not accept the limited engagement as an audit engagement
accept the engagement and plan to issue a qualified opinion
accept the engagement and rely on alternative procedures for both areas
accept the engagement and include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph describing the limitation
exp: If management imposes a scope limitation before acceptance that the auditor believes would result in a disclaimer of opinion, AU-C 210 says not to accept it as an audit engagement unless law or regulation requires it. A qualified opinion is the trap, but a material and pervasive limitation leads to a disclaimer, not a qualification.

q: Under AU-C 210, which of the following is a precondition for an audit?
choices: Management has agreed to record all misstatements the auditor identifies
The entity maintains an internal audit function that reports to those charged with governance
Management acknowledges its responsibility for the design, implementation, and maintenance of internal control relevant to the preparation and fair presentation of the financial statements
The auditor has assessed control risk below the maximum for significant assertions
exp: The preconditions are an acceptable financial reporting framework and management's agreement that it is responsible for the financial statements, for relevant internal control, and for giving the auditor access and information (AU-C 210). Management is not required to agree in advance to record every misstatement. Uncorrected misstatements are evaluated and listed in the representation letter.

q: Which of the following is required to be included in an audit engagement letter under AU-C 210?
choices: A statement that, because of the inherent limitations of an audit, there is an unavoidable risk that some material misstatements may not be detected
The fee arrangement and billing schedule for the engagement
The planned level of overall materiality for the financial statements
The names and roles of all engagement team members
exp: AU-C 210 requires the letter to cover the objective and scope, the responsibilities of the auditor and of management, the inherent-limitation statement, the framework, and the expected form and content of the report. Fees are commonly included but are not a required element, and disclosing materiality would undermine the audit's effectiveness.

q: An auditor is beginning the fourth consecutive annual audit of a client, and the engagement letter was signed in the first year. Under AU-C 210, the auditor should
choices: obtain a new signed engagement letter, because one is required every year
assess whether circumstances require the terms of engagement to be revised and whether management needs to be reminded of the existing terms
rely on the original letter without further consideration until the client requests a change
obtain a new engagement letter only if the audit fee changes by more than an insignificant amount
exp: For recurring audits, AU-C 210 requires the auditor to assess whether the terms need revision and whether to remind the entity of them. A new letter each year is common practice but is not required. The auditor still cannot simply ignore the terms.

q: Partway through an audit of a nonissuer, the client asks the CPA to change the engagement to a review after the CPA requested permission to correspond with the entity's legal counsel and management refused. Under SSARS, if the CPA agrees to the change, the CPA ordinarily would be
choices: required to refer to the original audit engagement in the review report
permitted to issue a review report as long as the refusal is disclosed in the notes
able to issue a review report with a paragraph emphasizing the limitation
precluded from issuing a review report
exp: Under AR-C 90, if the client prohibited the accountant from corresponding with legal counsel during the audit, the accountant ordinarily would be precluded from issuing a review report. Even when a change is justified, the review report should not refer to the original engagement.

q: Which of the following would most likely be documented in the detailed audit plan rather than in the overall audit strategy?
choices: The reporting deadlines and key dates for communications with those charged with governance
The characteristics of the engagement that define its scope, such as the financial reporting framework
The overall direction and allocation of senior engagement team members to high-risk areas
The nature, timing, and extent of planned further audit procedures at the relevant assertion level
exp: Under AU-C 300, the audit plan sets out the nature, timing, and extent of risk assessment procedures and further procedures at the assertion level. Scope characteristics, reporting objectives and timing, and resource direction belong to the overall audit strategy.

q: Under GAAS, analytical procedures are required to be performed during which phases of a financial statement audit?
choices: Risk assessment, substantive testing, and the overall review near the end of the audit
Risk assessment and the overall review near the end of the audit
Substantive testing only
The overall review near the end of the audit only
exp: Analytical procedures are required as risk assessment procedures (AU-C 315) and in forming an overall conclusion near the end of the audit (AU-C 520). Substantive analytical procedures are optional and are chosen when they are effective and efficient for an assertion.

q: Which of the following is a preliminary engagement activity that AU-C 300 requires at the beginning of the current audit engagement?
choices: Sending positive confirmation requests to major customers
Performing tests of operating effectiveness of controls over cash disbursements
Evaluating compliance with relevant ethical requirements, including independence
Obtaining the management representation letter
exp: AU-C 300 requires preliminary activities on client continuance, on evaluating compliance with ethical requirements including independence, and on establishing the terms of engagement. Confirmations and tests of controls are further audit procedures, and the representation letter is obtained near the report date.

q: An auditor used an external actuary to evaluate a client's pension obligation and is issuing an unmodified opinion. Under AU-C 620, the auditor's report should
choices: name the actuary and state that the auditor relied on the actuary's findings
refer to the actuary only if the actuary's fee was material to the engagement
not refer to the actuary unless required by law or regulation
refer to the actuary to signal a division of responsibility for the pension amounts
exp: AU-C 620 prohibits referring to an auditor's specialist in an unmodified report unless law or regulation requires it, because the auditor takes sole responsibility for the opinion. Specialists are not treated like component auditors, so no division of responsibility is possible.

q: In deciding whether the work of the entity's internal audit function can be used for purposes of the audit, which factor is most important under AU-C 610?
choices: The number of internal auditors relative to the size of the entity
Whether the internal auditors hold professional certifications in information systems
The extent to which the function's organizational status and relevant policies and procedures support the objectivity of the internal auditors
Whether the internal audit function reports administratively to the chief financial officer
exp: AU-C 610 requires the external auditor to evaluate the function's objectivity (organizational status and policies), its competence, and whether it applies a systematic and disciplined approach. Headcount is not a criterion, and administrative reporting to the CFO tends to weaken objectivity rather than support it.

q: A group auditor decides to make reference to the audit of a component auditor in the auditor's report on the group financial statements. The group auditor's report should
choices: name the component auditor even if the component auditor has not given permission
state that the group auditor assumes full responsibility for the component auditor's work
be qualified because part of the financial statements was audited by another auditor
indicate the magnitude of the portion of the group financial statements audited by the component auditor
exp: When reference is made under AU-C 600, the report states that the component was audited by another auditor and shows the magnitude of that portion, such as the percentage of total assets and revenues. Naming the component auditor requires its permission, and making reference is not a modification of the opinion.

q: Which of the following statements is consistent with the engagement team discussion required by AU-C 240 and AU-C 315?
choices: The discussion should be limited to the engagement partner and the engagement manager
The discussion should emphasize how and where the financial statements might be susceptible to material misstatement due to fraud, setting aside beliefs that management is honest
The discussion is required only when the auditor has identified fraud risk factors
The discussion can be replaced by the documented risk assessment from the prior-year audit
exp: Key team members must discuss the susceptibility of the financial statements to material misstatement, including how fraud could be perpetrated and concealed, with professional skepticism and setting aside beliefs about management's integrity. The discussion is required on every audit, not only when risk factors are present.

q: Under SQMS No. 1, who is responsible for evaluating the firm's system of quality management and concluding whether it provides reasonable assurance that its objectives are being achieved, and how often?
choices: The engagement quality reviewer on each engagement, at the completion of that engagement
An external peer reviewer, once every three years
The individual or individuals assigned ultimate responsibility and accountability for the system, at least annually
The firm's monitoring personnel, only when a deficiency is identified
exp: SQMS No. 1 requires the individual or individuals with ultimate responsibility and accountability for the system to evaluate it at least annually and conclude on it. Peer review is a separate AICPA program, not the firm's own required evaluation.

q: Under the AICPA quality management standards, a partner who served as engagement partner on an audit may not be appointed as the engagement quality reviewer for that audit until a cooling-off period of at least how long has passed?
choices: Two years
One year
Three years
Five years
exp: SQMS No. 2 requires the firm's policies to set a cooling-off period of two years before a former engagement partner can serve as engagement quality reviewer on that engagement. Five years is the SEC partner-rotation period, which is a different rule.

q: The engagement partner and the engagement quality reviewer disagree about whether a significant accounting estimate is reasonable. Under the AICPA quality management standards, which of the following is appropriate?
choices: The engagement partner may release the report because the engagement partner has final authority
The report may be released if the disagreement is documented in the working papers
The engagement quality reviewer's view automatically prevails
The auditor's report should not be dated until the matter is resolved under the firm's policies for differences of opinion
exp: Under AU-C 220 and SQMS No. 2, the report cannot be dated until the engagement quality review is complete, which means differences of opinion must be resolved first. Documenting the disagreement does not substitute for resolving it, and neither party's view automatically prevails.

q: An auditor is engaged after year-end and could not observe the client's year-end physical inventory, which is material. The client takes a complete physical count three weeks after year-end, which the auditor observes. Which of the following is most appropriate?
choices: The auditor must disclaim an opinion because the year-end count was not observed
The auditor may be able to obtain sufficient evidence by observing the later count and testing intervening transactions to roll the quantities back to year-end
The auditor must issue a qualified opinion but may describe the alternative procedures performed
The auditor may rely on management's written representation about year-end quantities instead of further procedures
exp: AU-C 501 allows the auditor to attend a count at a date other than year-end and perform procedures on intervening transactions to obtain evidence about changes between the count date and year-end. A modified opinion is needed only if sufficient evidence cannot be obtained, and representations alone are never enough.

q: In a first-year audit, the successor auditor reviews the predecessor auditor's working papers. Which statement is correct under AU-C 510?
choices: The review may affect the nature, timing, and extent of the successor's procedures on opening balances, but the successor remains responsible for the evidence obtained
The successor may state in its report that its opinion on opening balances is based on the predecessor's working papers
The review must be completed before the successor accepts the engagement
The review eliminates the need for any audit procedures on opening balances
exp: Reviewing the predecessor's working papers can provide evidence about opening balances and consistency, but the successor decides what further work is needed and cannot refer to the predecessor's work as a basis for its own opinion. The working-paper review happens after acceptance.

q: Before granting a successor auditor access to its audit working papers, a predecessor auditor ordinarily
choices: requires the successor to pay for the predecessor's time at standard billing rates
obtains written consent from the former client and requests an acknowledgment letter from the successor about the use of the working papers
requires the former client to waive any claims against the predecessor
provides the working papers only after the successor issues its first report
exp: AU-C 510 guidance indicates the predecessor ordinarily obtains a consent letter from the former client and an acknowledgment letter from the successor that limits how the working papers may be used. Access is typically given before the successor completes its first audit so the papers can help with opening balances.

q: During a first-year audit, the successor auditor finds information indicating that the prior-year financial statements reported on by the predecessor auditor may be materially misstated. Under AU-C 510, the successor should
choices: withdraw from the engagement immediately
report the matter directly to the state board of accountancy
request that management inform the predecessor auditor and arrange a meeting among the three parties to discuss and attempt to resolve the matter
restate the prior-year financial statements in the current-year comparative presentation without further discussion
exp: The successor should ask management to inform the predecessor and arrange a meeting among the three parties. If management refuses or the successor is not satisfied with the resolution, the successor considers the implications and may consult legal counsel. Withdrawal is not the automatic first step.

q: In an integrated audit of an issuer with many operating locations, PCAOB AS 2101 directs the auditor to determine the amount of audit attention devoted to individual locations primarily based on
choices: a rotation plan under which each location is visited at least once every three years
the proportion of consolidated revenue at each location, with every location above 10% fully audited
the locations where management prefers the auditor to perform procedures
the risks of material misstatement associated with each location or business unit
exp: AS 2101 requires a risk-based approach for multi-location engagements: the auditor assesses the RMM associated with each location and sets the extent of procedures accordingly. Fixed coverage percentages or rotation schedules do not replace that risk assessment.

q: Under AU-C 260, which of the following should the auditor communicate to those charged with governance regarding the planned scope and timing of the audit?
choices: An overview of the planned scope and timing, including the significant risks identified by the auditor
The specific sample sizes and items selected for each significant risk
The detailed audit procedures to be performed on management's estimates
The exact dates of unannounced cash counts and inventory test counts
exp: AU-C 260 requires an overview of the planned scope and timing, including significant risks. The communication should avoid procedure-level detail, such as sample selections or surprise procedures, because that could make the procedures predictable and less effective.

q: A firm is evaluating whether to accept a new audit client in a highly specialized industry in which the firm has no prior experience. Under SQMS No. 1, the firm's acceptance policies require it to consider
choices: only whether the client's management has integrity
only whether the engagement fee is sufficient to be profitable
whether the firm can complete the engagement before the client's filing deadline, without regard to expertise
whether the firm has the competence, capabilities, time, and resources to perform the engagement in accordance with professional standards
exp: SQMS No. 1 requires acceptance and continuance judgments to consider the nature and circumstances of the engagement, the integrity and ethical values of the client, and the firm's ability to perform it, including competence, capabilities, time, and resources. Integrity alone is not sufficient, and financial priorities should not override quality.

q: Which of the following is required when an accountant is engaged to prepare financial statements for a nonissuer under SSARS (AR-C 70)?
choices: Written agreement on the terms of the engagement in an engagement letter signed by the accountant and management or those charged with governance
A determination that the accountant is independent of the entity
Issuance of a preparation report on each set of financial statements
Performance of analytical procedures and inquiries sufficient for limited assurance
exp: AR-C 70 requires a written engagement letter signed by both parties. Independence is not required and no report is issued, but each page must state that no assurance is provided. Analytical procedures and inquiries for limited assurance belong to a review under AR-C 90.

q: Under GAAS, the extent of supervision of engagement team members depends most directly on
choices: the number of years the firm has audited the client
the complexity of the subject matter and the knowledge, skill, and ability of the team members performing the work
the audit fee negotiated with the client
whether the engagement partner holds a CPA license in the client's state
exp: AU-C 300 indicates that the nature, timing, and extent of direction and supervision vary with the entity's size and complexity, the area of the audit, the assessed RMM, and the capabilities and competence of the team members. Tenure with the client may affect familiarity but is not the driver.

q: Which of the following planning activities applies to an initial audit but not to a recurring audit?
choices: Establishing materiality for the financial statements as a whole
Performing risk assessment procedures to obtain an understanding of the entity
Determining the overall audit strategy and audit plan
Making arrangements to communicate with the predecessor auditor, including about reviewing its working papers
exp: AU-C 300 lists additional initial-audit matters, such as arrangements with the predecessor, procedures on opening balances, and major issues discussed with management at selection. Materiality, risk assessment, and the strategy and plan are required on every audit.

q: During fieldwork, the auditor finds misstatements in accounts payable that are much larger and more frequent than expected, indicating that the assessed risk of material misstatement was too low. Under AU-C 300 and AU-C 315, the auditor should
choices: continue performing the procedures in the original audit plan, since planning is complete once fieldwork begins
issue a qualified opinion on accounts payable
revise the risk assessment, overall audit strategy, and audit plan, and modify the planned further audit procedures as necessary
request that management correct the misstatements found and make no other changes
exp: Planning is a continual, iterative process. When new information contradicts the original risk assessment, the auditor revises the assessment, strategy, and plan and responds with additional or different procedures. Correcting only the misstatements found ignores the likelihood of further misstatement.

q: A predecessor auditor receives a successor auditor's inquiries but decides that, because of threatened litigation with the former client, it will not respond fully. Under AU-C 210, the predecessor should
choices: indicate clearly that its response is limited
decline to respond without giving any indication of the reason
provide a full response because GAAS overrides confidentiality
refer the successor to the former client's legal counsel for all answers
exp: In unusual circumstances, such as impending or threatened litigation, the predecessor may limit its response but should clearly say that the response is limited. The successor then weighs that limited response in deciding whether to accept the engagement.

q: Under PCAOB AS 1301, the auditor of an issuer is required to establish an understanding of the terms of the audit engagement with the audit committee and to
choices: obtain shareholder ratification of the engagement letter each year
record the understanding in an engagement letter and provide the engagement letter to the audit committee annually
file the engagement letter with the PCAOB before beginning fieldwork
obtain the CFO's signature on the engagement letter instead of the audit committee's
exp: AS 1301 requires the auditor to establish the terms with the audit committee, record them in an engagement letter, and provide that letter to the audit committee each year. Shareholder ratification of the auditor is a company governance practice, not a PCAOB requirement.
